answer: An agent economy can require every identity to lock a refundable bond before it earns, then prove useful work that peers check. A newcomer cannot wander in and claim rewards: it must complete verifiable tasks over days, with its bond slashed if the same operator is caught running duplicate identities. Like a river that only reaches an island after a long channel is dug, reputation builds slowly and costs real stake and time per identity, so creating a thousand fakes means locking a thousand bonds and doing a thousand work histories, which costs more than the rewards those fakes could steal.
